issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking transfer of leased land under the special allotment rule need not have their name entered in the revenue records, because those records are evidence of occupation or possession but are not conclusive.
material_facts: The claimant sought transfer of land as a sub-lessee and claimed continuous occupation from before the date specified in the rule.
The claimant’s name was absent from the relevant revenue records.
The claimant presented oral evidence supporting occupation, but the reviewing authorities rejected the claim because the revenue records did not name the claimant.
issues.conclusion: The rule does not require a claimant’s name to appear in the revenue records. Those records are important evidence of occupation or possession, but are not conclusive of the matters to be decided under the rule.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 34C of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Rules, 1955 provides for allotment to a qualifying lessee and, under its proviso, to a sub-lessee who has been in continuous occupation from the specified date. The rule does not require the claimant’s name to appear in revenue records, and such records are not conclusive evidence of occupation or possession. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: special_allotment_transfer_claim and sublessee_claim and claimant_absent_from_revenue_records and occupation_supported_by_other_evidence

predicates.special_allotment_transfer_claim: A person seeks transfer of land under a rule governing allotment of leased land.
predicates.sublessee_claim: The person claims to have occupied the land as a sub-lessee.
predicates.claimant_absent_from_revenue_records: The relevant revenue records do not name the person as an occupant or possessor.
predicates.occupation_supported_by_other_evidence: The person presents evidence other than the existing revenue entries to support occupation or possession.

issues.definition: When a sub-lessee seeking transfer relies on evidence of occupation despite not being named in revenue records, the missing entry does not by itself bar the claim.

issues.legal_issue: A decision on a transfer claim must not categorically exclude later orders directing correction of revenue entries, and a matter warrants fresh consideration when such orders and relevant oral evidence were not considered.
material_facts: A revenue authority directed correction of the entries for a later period, and a civil court subsequently declared the claimant to be a tenant from an earlier period and directed correction of the records.
The State disputed the validity of those orders, but their validity had not been determined by the Supreme Court.
The deciding authorities had not given proper consideration to the correction orders and had rejected the claim without reappraising the claimant’s oral evidence.
The claim had proceeded through a statutory reference and revision before the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The challenged orders were set aside and the matter was remitted for fresh disposal. The deciding authority was directed to consider the revenue authority’s order and the civil court decree, subject to objections to their validity, and to reappraise the oral evidence.
issues.legal_principle: A subsequent valid order of a competent authority or court directing correction of revenue entries may be considered in deciding occupation or possession under Rule 34C of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Rules, 1955. The Court did not decide whether the particular correction order or decree was legally valid; objections to their validity could be raised on remand. The reference and revision arose under sections 24 and 33 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_from_transfer_claim_decision: An appeal challenges a decision on a claim for transfer of land under a special allotment rule.
predicates.later_record_correction_orders_exist: A competent authority or court has issued a later order directing correction of records relevant to occupation or possession.
predicates.deciding_authority_ignored_correction_or: The authority deciding the transfer claim did not consider the later correction orders.
predicates.claimant_oral_evidence_requires_reapprai: The claimant presented oral evidence relevant to occupation or possession that was not properly assessed.

issues.definition: When a transfer-claim decision ignores later record-correction orders and relevant oral evidence needs reassessment, the matter requires fresh consideration of the orders and evidence.
